ideas.title: Ants on a honey road, in the game
ideas.critique: The swarm, the trail cutting the chord and the biscuit were already the film; what's new is the player drawing the scent and many small pulls adding up to a friction slide, and that only counts if the biscuit visibly creeps. A film that shows the trail forming again would be a repeat. The step is real when a played moment shows a crowd answering a hand-drawn line.

ideas.title: Knock on anything
same_form: The island answers a clap, a broken take
ideas.critique: Modal synthesis from each asset's own FEM eigenmodes is something no game here has done: the pitch of a note coming out of the shape, and changing when you carve the shape, is the real payoff. It is in the sound form, which already has two recent posts and had trouble showing on screen, so the visible mode shimmer has to carry the film.

ideas.title: Dig a river
ideas.critique: Terrain you can dig plus shallow water on a heightfield gives the island something it never had: water that reads the land the player shapes, and a goal that comes out of the simulation. The risk is in the engine change to the terrain mesh, and a trench film that shows no water finding a path would be just one more look.

ideas.title: Throw a pot
ideas.critique: Having the hands learn a skill is strong, and the slump from yield and buckling is a mechanism the island doesn't have. But an axisymmetric ring profile is a modest simulation, mouse sculpting at a wheel is a familiar minigame, and the wheel plus kiln add up to one more workshop place.

ideas.title: Tightrope over the lily pond
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Balance as a skill on a sagging, swinging rod chain is good drama to watch and to play, and the fall gives a payoff. Balance minigames are a well-known genre though, and it depends on Lumi's body actually reading as an inverted pendulum and not a tilting sprite.

ideas.title: A hot air balloon that steers by height
ideas.nearest: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Steering by finding the wind layer is a clever navigation rule, and the glowing envelope at dusk is a real path-tracer showpiece. Thermal buoyancy and a three-layer wind is a simple model, the balloon is another ride asset, and the dusk film could end up as only a pretty glow.

ideas.title: Sand castles against the tide
ideas.critique: MPM sand on the GPU where moisture decides cohesion is real new physics, and a tower slumping as a wave undercuts it is a moment people would clip. MPM at a scale you can play with live is risky, and if the tide only deletes the work this drifts toward wrecking with nothing to play.

ideas.title: A marble run down the hill
ideas.critique: Rolling contact with real spin on track meshes, plus a refractive marble, is solid physics and a good build-fail-retry loop. Marble runs are a very predictable toy, and the payoff (watch the machine run, chain reaction) is close to the domino run.

ideas.title: Lead the moths with a lantern
ideas.critique: The real dorsal-light-response rule, with its orbits and stalls, is a strange and true mechanic, and herding with your feet is a fresh puzzle. It is still a swarm answering a lure, right after the ants, and a night film of pale dots near a light risks looking like the fireflies take.

ideas.title: Shrink to ant size
ideas.critique: Physics changing with scale (surface tension, drag, dew lenses that focus light) is the real idea and very traceable. 'Become tiny' is an old game trope, the pitch rests on a lot of new near-ground geometry, and the most likely version is a scaled camera with a few special cases, not physics that holds wherever you look.
